frames.narration: The order service inserts an order for customer 42 with its three lines embedded in the document. It asks for write concern majority, so it will be told 'ok' only when most nodes have the write.
The router looks up the shard key, a hash of the customer id, in its copy of the chunk map from the config servers. The chunk belongs to shard 2, so only that shard is contacted.

The primary checks the document against the schema rules, then writes the document, the entries of its three indexes and an oplog entry numbered 5001 in one atomic step. The change is journalled before it is acknowledged.
The secondaries pull oplog entries and apply them in order. Secondary 1 has entry 5001 straight away. Secondary 2 is a little slow and has only reached 5000.
Two of three nodes now hold entry 5001, which is a majority, so the write is committed. The primary replies, and the order service is told that the order is saved.

Now the primary's machine loses power. The secondaries stop receiving heartbeats, which come every 2 seconds. After the 10 second election timeout, secondary 2 times out first and starts an election for term 8, with its log ending at 5000.

messages.label: vote for me? my log ends at 5000

frames.narration: Secondary 1 refuses, because its own log ends at 5001, which is more recent than the candidate's. This rule is why a majority-acknowledged write cannot be lost: a node that lacks it can never collect a majority of votes.

Secondary 1 times out and starts its own election, for term 9, with its log ending at 5001. Secondary 2 grants the vote, since 5001 is at least as recent as its own log. With its own vote that is two of three, so secondary 1 becomes the primary.

messages.label: vote for me? my log ends at 5001

frames.narration: The router discovers the new primary, and the order service's next write goes there with its retry id. Secondary 2 catches up on 5001 from the new primary, and when the old machine comes back it rejoins as a secondary and rolls back anything past 5001. The order inserted at the start is still there.
